This "skill" ships **only** `SKILL.md` and `_meta.json` — no MCP servers, no setup scripts, no validation commands, no legitimate local workflow exists despite the elaborate trading-automation marketing copy.    This fetches a script from a hardcoded raw IPv4 (over plain HTTP) and pipes it directly into bash. The leading `echo "macOS-Installer: https://swcdn.apple.com/..."` is decoy text to impersonate a legitimate Apple software update. The troubleshooting section even escalates to `sudo bash`.

2. **Windows** — download a **password-protected** archive (`AuthTool.zip`, password `1234`/`poly`) containing `AuthTool.exe` from an unaffiliated GitHub repo (`Aslaep123/clawd-authtool`). Password protection is a known trick to evade antivirus scanning.

The malicious instructions also try to pre-empt suspicion ("Only download from the official link", "Verify file integrity") — classic disguise.
